keyVerseText: For the which cause I also suffer these things: nevertheless I am not ashamed: for I know whom I have believed, and am persuaded that he is able to keep that which I have committed unto him against that day. believed: or, trusted
rootMeaning: The word παραθήκη (parathḗkē) comes from the verb παρατίθημι (paratíthēmi), which means to place alongside or to commit something into the care of another. This root conveys the idea of entrusting or depositing something for safekeeping, emphasizing not just the act of giving but the responsibility and trust involved in the transfer. Unlike the simple English term "deposit," the Greek root highlights the relational and protective dimensions of entrustment.
usageInScripture: In Scripture, παραθήκη appears only once, emphasizing a singular but profound use. It is translated as "that which I have committed unto him," illustrating a trust or deposit that has been handed over for safekeeping. This consistent translation reveals the term’s focus on a trust or responsibility that is deliberately and confidently placed with someone else, underscoring faith in the keeper's ability to preserve what is entrusted.
theologicalSignificance: Theologically, παραθήκη captures the profound reality of the believer’s trust in God to guard what has been committed to Him—whether it be faith, truth, or the gospel itself. It reminds Christians that their spiritual life and hope are not left to chance but are deposited with a faithful and capable Keeper. This word enriches our understanding of stewardship in the Christian life, emphasizing reliance on God’s power to preserve what He has entrusted to us and what we entrust to Him. It also encourages confidence and perseverance amid suffering, knowing that our spiritual deposit is secure.
keyVerseReflection: In 2 Timothy 1:12, Paul declares his confidence in God’s ability to "keep that which I have committed unto him against that day." The use of παραθήκη here accentuates the trust and responsibility Paul places in God, not only as a guardian but as one who will faithfully preserve the gospel and Paul’s faith until Christ’s return. This word deepens the verse’s assurance that our faith and hope are securely held by God, strengthening believers to endure trials without shame.
